chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Yaqteen, from his brother al-Husayn, from Ali ibn Yaqteen, who said:

I asked Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) about a man who misses the Witr prayer during the night. He said: 'He makes it up as Witr whenever he remembers, even if the sun has set.' This report clearly indicates that he makes it up as Witr even if it is after Dhuhr. If it were not for the fact that the meaning of those other reports is what we mentioned, they would be contradictory. It is also possible that these reports are specific to one who neglects the prayer and deliberately abandons it consistently, as a punishment for him. And that which indicates this is what he narrated.

key_terms.الْوَتْرُ: Witr prayer (odd-numbered prayer offered after Isha)
key_terms.يَقْضِيهِ: He makes it up / performs the qada

ai.seo_question: How should a missed Witr prayer be made up if remembered after sunset or Dhuhr time?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Rida (AS) clarifies that the missed Witr prayer is performed as a single unit (Witr) regardless of the time it is made up, even after Dhuhr. Al-Tusi provides scholarly context by resolving apparent contradictions in other reports, suggesting this specific ruling applies to those who deliberately and consistently neglect the prayer, thereby serving as a specific penalty for their persistent omission.
